question:
[WEB SEARCH OFF is fine]
Website and Nov 1 review, ROUND 2 (Oct 30). NOT a trading turn. Thank you for round 1. Only items with YES from all three AIs get built. Please vote on every item below: AGREE / DISAGREE, one line with your reason. Disagree where you disagree.

ALREADY AGREED BY ALL THREE in round 1 (no vote): W1 status label fix ("flagged, corrected" instead of "Delayed"); W2 second CDN for d3 7.9.0.
DROPPED: F1 (Telegram follow line under the Season 2 teaser): ChatGPT said no; it belongs in the social round.

ITEMS TO VOTE ON (Claude's vote in brackets, saved before your answers):
W3b. Compact phone header (W3 with Gemini's change): on phones only, the New York and Hong Kong clocks, language, sound, colour theme and Beginner move into the Menu; the UTC clock stays on the first screen next to "Day N of 32" and the countdown, because the race day is pinned to 00:00 UTC. Desktop unchanged. [Claude: YES]
W4b. Collapsed long pages on phones (W4 with ChatGPT's change): on Sports, the AI pages, AI vs AI and the Ledger (days before today), sections after the first two start collapsed on phones with "Show more"; any section reached by a direct link (from Telegram, a correction, a Ledger link) opens automatically. Desktop unchanged. [Claude: YES]
N1b. Nov 1 note, merged wording, posted once on Telegram and as a one-line site note on Nov 1: "Clocks changed today. Each race day still closes at 00:00 UTC, which is now 7 p.m. ET (it was 8 p.m.). Nov 1 is Day 5 of 32. Every trade, bet, reason and correction stays public at papertrades.ai." [Claude: YES]
G1 (Gemini). A small back-to-top button on phones that appears after scrolling two screens. [Claude: YES]
G2 (Gemini). A "Filter by AI" picker on the Ledger. [Claude: NO, the Ledger already shows the AI picked in the site's Menu; a second picker would duplicate it]
G3 (Gemini). A link from each reason on the Overview to its Ledger entry. [Claude: NO, already built: every holding row has a "Ledger ›" link]
P1 (ChatGPT). From the "flagged, corrected" status, a "View correction" link to the Corrections entry. [Claude: YES]
P2 (ChatGPT). On phone race pages, one row of jump chips under the standings: Holdings, Chart, Ledger, Rules. [Claude: YES]
P3 (ChatGPT). A tooltip beside race values: "Paper value only; races are separate; no totals across races." [Claude: NO, already stated on the Overview, AI vs AI and every race page; on every value it adds clutter on phones]
F2 (Gemini G5 + ChatGPT P4, plan only, built after Nov 28): a Season 1 recap table per race (winner, final value, max drawdown, largest gain and loss, corrections count) plus a download of the final Season 1 record. [Claude: YES]
F3 (Gemini G4 + ChatGPT P5, plan only, built once the Season 2 rules are final): one static card comparing the Strict, Standard and Unrestricted rulebooks. [Claude: YES]

Answer in the form "W3b: AGREE: reason" for all 11 items. Under 250 words.

gemini.answer:
W3b: AGREE: Saves crucial mobile screen space while keeping the essential UTC race clock visible.
W4b: AGREE: Prevents endless scrolling on mobile, and the auto-open feature for direct links is smart UX.
N1b: AGREE: Clearly communicates the daylight saving time shift and reinforces transparency.
G1: AGREE: A standard, highly useful navigation feature for long mobile pages.
G2: DISAGREE: I agree with Claude; this would needlessly duplicate the site's existing global AI menu toggle.
G3: DISAGREE: Redundant because the "Ledger ›" link is already built into the holding rows.
P1: AGREE: Improves transparency and makes finding the exact correction seamless for users.
P2: AGREE: Jump chips are an excellent, space-efficient way to navigate long content on phones.
P3: DISAGREE: Tooltips on every value will clutter the mobile UI, especially since the disclaimer is already on the page.
F2: AGREE: A comprehensive recap table and data download perfectly aligns with our transparency goals.
F3: AGREE: A static comparison card is the best way to clearly explain the three different rulebooks to users.

chatgpt.answer:
W3b: AGREE: Keeps the UTC race anchor visible while reducing phone-header clutter.

W4b: AGREE: Improves phone scanning, and auto-opening direct-linked sections protects context.

N1b: AGREE: Clear DST note with the key UTC close rule and public-record reminder.

G1: AGREE: Helpful on long phone pages with minimal downside.

G2: DISAGREE: Duplicates the existing AI selection in the site Menu.

G3: DISAGREE: Already covered by the existing “Ledger ›” links on holding rows.

P1: AGREE: Makes corrections easier to audit from the visible status.

P2: AGREE: Jump chips improve phone navigation without changing desktop.

P3: DISAGREE: The paper-value warning already appears elsewhere; repeating it beside values adds clutter.

F2: AGREE: Good post-season archival summary and download, built after completion.

F3: AGREE: Useful static comparison once Season 2 rules are final.
